chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
title: Baby Dodds and reading versus playing your own way
summary: He speaks of Baby Dodds and says great players like Bix played their own way.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, how did Baby Dodge rate in those days? When you were down in New Orleans?

Well, Baby Dodge... He played with... What Fade Merrill was banned before Zutty and those guys... Played on... On the Sidney. Mm-hmm. When Louis Armstrong played with the band, you know? Mm-hmm. And he... He played... New Orleans drums. I don't know whether he could read or not. I mean...

In those days... In those days, New Orleans musicians... None of them cared anything about reading. No. They played jazz music, you know... Ragtime music or whatever you want to call it. And they played it their own way. Mm-hmm. But today, it's a different world. Music has advanced so much that... Mm-hmm. They got all these guys there to write things out... And you play with Stan if you're right the wrong note. They play the wrong note. You know what I mean? It's about as much feeling as a piece of wood. Oh, yeah.
And no sense. Mm-hmm. Just like Bix... Bix played his chorus as his way.
I mean, Bix wasn't the greatest reader in the world. No.

I mean, he played his chorus as his way... And... And... Things like that. I mean, all the great guys that... That... That... That... That you can... I can mention. They all play their own way and they're not the greatest reader... Because they didn't want to play all that stuff. Yeah. All they're doing... All they're doing is playing something somebody else wrote. Anybody can play. Any good... Good music... Uh... Read music fast and... And... Can play anything that you put in front of them. Yeah. But tell them to play something of their own. They can't do it. Yeah. Well... They wouldn't know which way to tell them with their horns. You know what I mean?
Yeah. Well... I... I always like that saying... Can you read? Yeah, but not enough to hurt my playing.
